scope: Bounded fictional service-level checks, not independent calibration or browser acceptance

proposal.title: Understand fractions and compare equal shares in everyday situations
proposal.reason: This unreviewed generated preview uses five approximately twenty-minute modules with visual examples and simple English explanations, without assuming your starting skill level.

modules.title: Recognise wholes and equal shares in everyday pictures
modules.reason: A fraction describes equal parts of a whole, so recognising fair divisions supports every later comparison.
modules.outcome: You will correctly identify the whole and distinguish equal from unequal divisions in four out of five pictured examples.

modules.title: Connect fraction symbols with shaded parts of pictures
modules.reason: Connecting symbols with pictures helps you describe how many equal parts exist and how many are selected.
modules.outcome: You will match halves, thirds, quarters, and eighths to pictures and explain both numbers correctly in four out of five examples.

modules.title: Compare shares with matching denominators or matching numerators
modules.reason: These comparisons show why more same-sized parts give a larger share, while dividing a whole into more parts makes each part smaller.
modules.outcome: You will use shaded strips to compare fractions sharing a denominator or numerator, correctly answering four out of five comparisons involving equal-sized wholes.

modules.title: Recognise equivalent fractions by dividing matching visual strips
modules.reason: Equivalent fractions explain how different numbers can describe the same amount and make unlike fractions easier to compare.
modules.outcome: You will show that one half equals two quarters and four eighths, then correctly match three additional pictured equivalent pairs.

modules.title: Apply fraction comparisons to everyday sharing and choices
modules.reason: Comparing food portions, shared materials, and filled containers connects fraction reasoning with practical decisions about equal shares.
modules.outcome: You will correctly solve four out of five everyday comparisons, using equivalent fractions or pictures and explaining when different whole sizes prevent a direct comparison.

proposal.outcome: You will compare everyday shares using pictures, fraction symbols, and simple explanations, while checking that the wholes are the same size.

diagnostic.prompt: Which division makes four equal shares of one sandwich?
options: Four pieces that each contain the same amount
Four pieces with one larger than the others
Four pieces with two larger than the others

diagnostic.prompt: A strip has four equal sections, with one shaded; which fraction describes the shaded amount?
In the fraction two fifths, what does the five tell you?
options: The number of equal parts that are selected
The number of equal parts in the whole
The number of separate wholes that are selected

diagnostic.prompt: Two equal-sized pizzas are cut into quarters; which share contains more pizza?
options: Both shares contain the same amount

diagnostic.prompt: Two people each receive half a cake; what information lets you decide whether they receive equal amounts?
options: Whether the cakes have the same whole size
Whether the cakes have the same icing colour
Whether the cakes are served on matching plates
